OG-15.from: In a grid-down winter scenario, hypothermia is a real threat within hours — not days. A warm home is not just about comfort; it is about survival.
OG-15.to: In a winter power cut, a cold home can become a health risk — especially for babies, older people and anyone with a health condition. A warm, dry home is about health, not just comfort.
OG-15.reason: Owner ruling 5.1 and 5.2: no official source gives 'within hours' for a cold home (removed); 'about survival' replaced with the owner's wording. Groups at risk: Health NZ and Better Health Channel (Vic).

OG-15.where: Heating cost reality check — claims 4 and 5
OG-15.from: Every 1°C you lower your thermostat saves approximately 10% on heating bills. A home heated to 21°C costs roughly 30% more than one heated to 18°C.
OG-15.to: Each extra degree of heating uses more energy, so heat to a healthy temperature rather than a higher one.
OG-15.reason: Owner rulings 5.4 and 5.5: the '10%' overstates energy.gov.au (5–10%) and EECA gives no percentage, so the statement is non-numeric; the derived '30%' claim is removed.

OG-11.from: Build a 30-day food supply that your family will actually eat.
OG-11.to: Build toward a 30-day pantry that your family will actually eat.
OG-11.reason: 30 days is OffGrid056's planning goal, not an official requirement (owner ruling 1); 'build toward' makes it a goal.

OG-11.from: Target: 30 days of calories per person (approx. 2,000 cal/day = 60,000 calories per person for 30 days).
OG-11.to: Build beyond the basic emergency supply toward a pantry target that suits your household, storage space, budget and resilience goals. OffGrid056's planning goal is 30 days. The official emergency baseline in New Zealand is food for at least three days (Get Ready).
OG-11.reason: Separates the official baseline (Get Ready NZ: 'stuck at home for three days or more', read live) from the optional 30-day goal. Removes the calorie figures: 'cal' is not the unit on NZ labels (kilojoules), and the 8,700 kJ reference was not found on the FSANZ page read.

OG-11.from: Target: 30 days of calories per person (approx. 2,000 cal/day = 60,000 calories per person for 30 days).
OG-11.to: Build beyond the basic emergency supply toward a pantry target that suits your household, storage space, budget and resilience goals. OffGrid056's planning goal is 30 days. Official emergency advice varies by state — from food for at least three days (Get Ready Queensland) to supplies for up to 14 days (NSW Food Authority) — so check your state's advice.
OG-11.reason: AU baseline is state-based: Get Ready Queensland 'Non-perishable food for three days' and NSW Food Authority 'sufficient supply … for up to 14 days' (both read live). No single national figure is implied.

OG-11.from: Most canned goods last 2–5 years. Dried goods last 1–2 years. Write expiry dates clearly on every item with a permanent marker. Check your pantry every 3 months. Use what expires soonest — this is the rotation principle covered in OG-12.
OG-11.to: Check the date on every item. A use-by date is about safety: don't eat food after it. A best-before date is about quality: food should still be safe for a while after it, but may not be at its best. Some canned foods with a shelf life of more than two years carry no date — write the date you bought them on the can with a permanent marker. Inspect cans as you go and don't use any that are swollen, leaking, rusted or dented. Check your pantry regularly and use what expires soonest first — the 'first in, first out' rotation principle.
OG-11.reason: Replaces unsourced shelf lives (2–5 years, 1–2 years) with FSANZ's use-by / best-before rules and can guidance (read live; FSANZ covers both NZ and AU). 'Every 3 months' → 'regularly' (NSW Food Authority: dates 'checked regularly'). Removes the OG-12 reference.

'Under 20°C' is unsourced; FSANZ: canned foods keep best 'in a cool, dry place'. 'Dry' is already its own checklist item, so the line is simply 'Cool' — the longer wording wrapped its cell across a page break.

OG-11.from: Add 2–3 extra items per weekly grocery run. In 10 weeks, you have a full 30-day supply without stressing your budget.
OG-11.to: Add a few extra items to each weekly shop. Over time you will reach your pantry target without stressing your budget.
OG-11.reason: '2–3 items → 30 days in 10 weeks' is arithmetic that depends entirely on what is bought; non-numeric instead.
